subject.title: Group chat context handling can blur which messages are addressed to the current agent

question: Should OpenClaw add durable target-aware group-history and reply metadata for multi-agent Telegram groups, or treat current prompt/current-turn mention facts as the intended boundary for now?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent API shape depends on maintainer intent around sibling-bot identity discovery, ambient versus other-bot semantics, and whether core history contracts should grow for this use case.

options.title: Approve Target-Aware Metadata
options.body: Define and implement per-message target facts in core history/reply context and populate them from Telegram where reliable, with tests and live proof.

options.title: Use Prompt-Only Mitigation
options.body: Accept the narrower prompt/docs path as an interim or final mitigation while leaving group history flat.

options.title: Keep It Channel-Specific
options.body: Avoid growing core history contracts and require channel or external plugin workflows to handle richer multi-agent attribution.

recommendation.title: Approve Target-Aware Metadata
recommendation.body: Define and implement per-message target facts in core history/reply context and populate them from Telegram where reliable, with tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram group-history and inbound addressing commits make obviyus the strongest current-code routing candidate for the product/API decision.
